task_retrieval_key:
An 81-year-old man initially developed a cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath. He was first treated with azithromycin for bronchitis, followed by levofloxacin after a right upper lobe infiltrate was found. His symptoms progressed despite antibiotics. Medical history includes coronary artery disease with coronary artery bypass (two years prior), atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c: 8.1%). He had spent time at a Northern Minnesota cabin but reported minimal outdoor exposure. Previous missionary work in Colombia ended two years before admission. Never smoked and rarely consumed alcohol.
Vital signs: Temperature 38.6°C, Pulse 130 beats/min, Blood Pressure 114/61 mm Hg, Respiratory Rate 22 breaths/min, Oxygen Saturation 82% (improved to >90% with 5 L/min oxygen). Lung sounds were diminished in the right upper lobe, with diffuse crackles in the right lung base. No clubbing or cyanosis. Cardiac examination showed tachycardic irregularly irregular rhythm, systolic ejection murmur, and mild pitting edema to the knee bilaterally. No cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy. Neurologic and skin examinations were normal. Later developed right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with an asymmetrically miotic right pupil (more evident in dark environment).
